title: Sample section — all item types
source: Original demo items (not from any test publisher)

questions.prompt: The lab notebook was so (i)________ that a new teammate could rerun every trial without asking a single question, yet the prose stayed (ii)________ enough that it never felt like a manual.
questions.explanation: Rerunning trials without questions → meticulous. Not like a manual → readable.

questions.prompt: Because the archive had no index, the intern's search was necessarily ________: she opened boxes at random and hoped a label would appear.
questions.explanation: No index + random boxes → haphazard / desultory.

questions.passage_label: Question 3 is based on this passage.
questions.passage: City orchardists used to spray weekly. After a dry spring, they switched to watering only when leaf-curl appeared. Fruit size dropped, but fungal spots nearly vanished. The growers concluded that less water, not less spray, caused the cleaner fruit.
questions.prompt: Which finding most weakens the growers' conclusion?
options: (A) Leaf-curl is more common after wet springs than dry ones.
(B) The new schedule also cut the number of spray days in half.
(C) Fruit size is mainly set in the first three weeks after bloom.
(D) Nearby gardens that kept weekly spraying had larger fruit.
(E) Customers prefer unmarked fruit even when it is smaller.
questions.explanation: If spraying also fell, the cleaner fruit may be from less spray, not less water.

questions.prompt: Which of the following must be even? Indicate all that apply.
questions.explanation: $2k$ is even. $k(k+1)$ is two consecutive integers, so even.
